svg.text: COPPER SIDE, mirrored: what you see when you cut the tracks
50 × 14 holes · cut to 127.0 × 35.6 mm · 29 cuts · 26 links · 2 standoff holes (2.5 mm, for M2.5 nylon standoffs)
Buffer the guitar (about 1 MΩ in) and pad Line by −9.7 dB.
C2 100µF 25V — + on row 1, stripe on row 0
C4 10µF 50V — + on row 4, stripe on row 5
R1 100Ω — with C2, the supply filter — it lives here, not on the 9 V board
R5 680k — 680 kΩ, the top of the Line pad
R6 330k — 330 kΩ, the shunt to the bias
U1 OPA2197 — pin 1 at the top left. The spare half is a follower on the
Connectors (pin 1 is the large filled square)
A2 → Bypass relay, JST-XH 2-way (B2B-XH-A): 1 GND · 2 TIP, to the input
A3 → Inst/Line toggle, JST-XH 3-way (B3B-XH-A): 1 SW-I · 2 SW-C · 3 SW-L
No ground: its three wires are the 1 MΩ node, not a ground.
A4 → Codec carrier, JST-XH 4-way (B4B-XH-A): 1 GND · 2 LIN1 · 3 GND · 4 +9
GND reaches the root through A4 only (Codec carrier).
The op-amp and its supply sit where they do on board 1. The connectors are
new, and so is the filter: R1 and C2 have moved here from the 9 V board.
Mount it directly behind the IN jack and the toggle. The toggle’s three
wires are the 1 MΩ node, and in the first test they were 14 dB of the hum,
so keep them as short as the panel allows.
SW-I and SW-C are the same node and are not joined on the board. The toggle
joins them. At Line, pin 3 to the bias reads 330 kΩ; at Inst, 1.01 MΩ.
Ground arrives on A4, with the signal and the supply, and that is this

Red ✕: cut the track at that hole (red bar: cut between two holes). Lines: wire links on the component side (green carries ground). Strips tinted green carry ground, red a supply, amber 3.3 V. White circles: standoff holes; dashed: what the standoff covers.
